extraction.name: OpenBookQA
extraction.description: OpenBookQA is a question answering dataset modeled after open book exams for assessing human understanding of a subject. It consists of 5,957 multiple-choice elementary-level science questions paired with an 'open book' core set of 1,326 science facts and an auxiliary set of about 6,000 additional facts. Answering the questions requires multi-hop reasoning combining a core science fact with broad common knowledge.
extraction.creator: Todor Mihaylov, Peter Clark, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal
extraction.citeAs: Mihaylov, T., Clark, P., Khot, T., & Sabharwal, A. (2018). Can a Suit of Armor Conduct Electricity? A New Dataset for Open Book Question Answering. In Proceedings of the 2018 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP) / arXiv:1809.02789.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A multi-stage crowdsourcing process where crowd-workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk are shown a random science fact from a filtered set of WorldTree facts, think of a second common fact to derive a new assertion, convert it into a 4-way multiple-choice question with 3 distractors, pass basic checks, test hardness using an IR solver and word-association solver, and verify answerability with 5 new crowd-workers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: A subset of the WorldTree corpus (specifically 1,326 facts filtered from 2,287 facts marked as 'central' by Jansen et al., 2018) and crowd-generated questions and additional facts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Basic automated checks ensuring exactly 4 choices, absence of negative words (no, none, not, etc.), and uniform answer choice length (all choices with at most 3 or at least 4 words). Adversarial filtering using an IR solver and a word association solver (ensuring neither answers correctly and top 3 IR sentences are insufficient). Answerability verification by crowd-workers requiring 4 out of 5 to answer correctly (discarding 2,183 out of 8,140 questions). Random shuffling of answer choices to eliminate answer position bias. Expert filtering on Dev and Test sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-workers generated questions and distractor choices given a core science fact and a common knowledge fact. For answerability verification, questions were shown to 5 independent crowd-workers who answered the 4-way multiple-choice question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were retained only if at least 4 out of 5 workers answered them correctly in crowdsourcing step 7. Out of 8,140 questions collected, 2,183 were discarded. Dev and Test sets were further inspected and filtered by an in-house expert.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk crowd-workers located in North America with a 'masters' level qualification.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Inherent human bias in crowdsourced questions where distractors may share common properties or non-scientific terms making plausible answer detectors (choice-only) and odd-one-out baselines achieve ~50% accuracy. Originally, choice 'A' was the correct answer in 69% of questions prior to random shuffling. In 21% of examined questions, the question did not strictly require the core science fact.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The additional facts (K) provided by crowd workers are often noisy, incomplete, over-complete, or only distantly related to the question. Models trained on the training set may fail when questions drift toward distant non-science domains (e.g., law/court cases) or involve complex choices such as 'all of these' or negative reasoning ('all but').
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of multi-hop question answering systems, open book QA models, and knowledge-enhanced reasoning systems. Split into 4,957 Train, 500 Dev, and 500 Test questions.
